label: DAILY EDITION
title: Three things worth knowing
subtitle: A lower cancer-risk association after appendectomy, faster X-59 flight testing and a ratified pay deal for 17,000 Boeing workers.

stories.title: 30,000-case analysis linked appendectomy to 58% lower colorectal-cancer risk
stories.text: Among 15,774 people who had surgery for acute appendicitis, 0.7% were later diagnosed with colorectal cancer, compared with 1.7% of 15,295 people treated with antibiotics alone.
stories.why: The result identifies a possible long-term factor for treatment discussions and follow-up. It is an observational conference analysis, cannot prove that surgery prevented cancer and is not a recommendation for everyone with appendicitis to have an operation.

stories.title: NASA’s X-59 completed six test flights in one week and reached Mach 1.53
stories.text: The quiet-supersonic research aircraft beat its previous weekly record by two flights, reached about 1,010 mph and brought its total to 38 test flights.
stories.why: The higher test tempo advances work on supersonic flight with quieter sonic thumps. Community-response surveys and any regulatory change still lie ahead, and the aircraft has entered roughly three weeks of scheduled maintenance.

stories.title: 17,000 Boeing workers ratified a four-year contract with an immediate 10% raise
stories.text: The agreement also provides annual 4% raises and a possible additional 2% based on performance, after both professional and technical bargaining units approved it.
stories.why: The deal delivers a substantial pay increase and averts a strike that could have disrupted aircraft certification and deliveries. Support was not overwhelming—53% in the technical unit—and the union says deeper trust and engineering-culture problems remain.
